instructions: Fill a large pot with water, add 2 tsp of the salt and put it on high heat. While it heats, slice the mushrooms, chop the shallot, mince the garlic, grate the Parmesan and chop 2 tbsp of parsley.
Add the rigatoni to the boiling water and cook for about 11 minutes, until al dente. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage, breaking it up, and cook for 5 minutes, until browned. Transfer it to a bowl and leave the fat in the pan.
Add the mushrooms and 1/4 tsp of the salt to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes without stirring much, until they are browned and the liquid has cooked off.
Add the shallot and cook for 1 minute. Add the garlic, thyme and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Cook for 1 minute, until it has mostly cooked off.
Return the sausage to the pan. Add the cream and the pepper and simmer for 2 minutes, until the sauce thickens slightly.
Take the pan off the heat. Add the pasta and the Parmesan and toss, adding a splash of the pasta water until the sauce coats the pasta.
Scatter the parsley over the top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Honest time is 30 minutes, with the sauce made while the pasta boils. The lead is a cream sauce with sausage, mushrooms, shallot and wine; the other versions (Closet Cooking, All Cooked Up) bring in tomato, so I added tomato paste cooked into the base for a light tomato cream, which the lead does not use. I left out the dried porcini to keep to the time. Skinny Spatula's rating is as shown on the page; the page text did not show the JSON-LD.
